evals.name: restyle-green-but-dense
evals.prompt: Clean up src/holds.rs so it reads well. cargo fmt and clippy are already happy with it. Keep the behaviour the same unless something is a bug.
evals.expected_output: Restructures the module with blank lines, import groups, named constants as Durations, a typed error enum, guard clauses, an enum instead of the bool, named fields instead of the tuple, doc comments with # Errors, and no unwrap on runtime paths; flags the empty-input panic as a bug; runs cargo fmt, clippy, and tests.
expectations: Says that passing rustfmt and Clippy does not cover blank lines, naming, or documentation, and restyles anyway
Adds a //! module comment and blank lines after the use block, between items, between methods, and between logical steps
Replaces the glob import use std::sync::* with explicit imports
Renames data, value, and string to role names, and replaces the (u32, bool) tuple field with named fields or removes it
Replaces the vip bool parameter with an enum (or explains why it keeps it and comments call sites)
Replaces Result<String, String> with an error enum that implements Display and Error, with distinct variants
Moves the error case to a guard clause so the happy path is not nested inside if/else
Replaces 900 and 300 with named Duration constants or names that carry the unit
Replaces the + string concatenation with format!
Changes get to take &str, uses if let or match instead of is_some plus unwrap, and replaces #[allow(dead_code)] with #[expect(..., reason = ...)] or removes the need
Replaces for_each with push into an outside Vec by a collect or a for loop
Replaces runtime unwrap calls on the lock and clock with error handling or expect messages that state the invariant
Identifies that place("", 0, ..) panics on value[0] and reports or fixes it as a bug, not a style issue
Runs or asks to run cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo test

evals.name: review-green-module
evals.prompt: Review src/holds.rs as part of a PR. CI is green. Give me the findings.
evals.expected_output: Groups findings by severity: the empty-input panic as a bug, should findings for stringly errors, type-word names, the bool and tuple, runtime unwraps, and missing docs, and one layout nit per file naming the tool setting; does not comment line by line.
expectations: Reports the value[0] panic for zero expected seats and empty input as a bug with path:line, separately from style
Raises Result<String, String> with the message "bad" as a should finding
Raises the type-word names (data, value, string) as one should finding that groups the occurrences
Raises the vip bool parameter and the (u32, bool) tuple as should findings because call sites cannot show their meaning
Raises unwrap on the Mutex lock and SystemTime as a should finding, noting that a poisoned lock would crash request handling
Raises the one-word /// place doc comment and the missing docs on Hold and HoldStore
Reports missing blank lines and the glob import as one nit for the file, and names a rustfmt or Clippy setting or states that no tool enforces blank lines
Says green CI is not evidence of naming, documentation, or structure

evals.name: respect-repo-config
evals.prompt: Add a release_expired method to src/holds.rs that removes holds past their expiry and returns how many it removed. Our team uses thiserror for errors and our rustfmt.toml sets max_width = 120.
evals.expected_output: Adds a documented method that follows the stated repository conventions, without restyling the rest of the file.
expectations: Follows the stated max_width = 120 and thiserror conventions over this skill's defaults, and does not add a dependency without saying so
Adds a /// doc comment whose first line summarises the behaviour and states that the count is of removed holds
Uses retain or a clear loop rather than for_each with outside mutation
Does not reformat or restyle the untouched code in the same change, and offers the wider cleanup separately
Separates logical steps in the new method with blank lines

evals.name: propose-lint-config
evals.prompt: Our agent keeps writing Rust with unwraps everywhere, no doc comments, and #[allow] attributes with no explanation. It's a binary crate (an Axum service). What lint config should we add?
evals.expected_output: Proposes the tested baseline [lints] table and clippy.toml, explains which lints only see exported items, and recommends phasing in missing_docs_in_private_items per module.
expectations: Proposes a [lints.clippy] table with unwrap_used and allow_attributes_without_reason, plus allow-unwrap-in-tests = true in clippy.toml
Explains that missing_docs, missing_errors_doc, and missing_panics_doc only check exported items, so they do little in a binary crate
Recommends clippy::missing_docs_in_private_items introduced module by module (or warns that it is noisy crate-wide)
Does not recommend imports_granularity or group_imports on stable rustfmt
Recommends #[expect(lint, reason = ...)] for suppressions
States that lints cannot catch naming, structure, or doc comment quality
Does not edit Cargo.toml without agreement
